root.title: Upgrading & Jailbreaking Help
root.body:
If you upgrade iOS with iTunes, your device will be un-jailbroken and Cydia packages will be deleted. Before upgrading iOS, make sure a jailbreak is available for the new version.

As of September 8, 2015

No jailbreak for 8.4.1

Currently there is no jailbreak for iOS 8.4.1. Avoid upgrading or restoring if you want a jailbroken device.

If you want to wipe all data on your device without upgrading the iOS, consider trying Cydia Impactor.

For frequently updated news, see /r/jailbreak on Reddit.

Untethered jailbreak for 8.1.3-8.4

TaiG has released an untethered jailbreak for iOS 8.1.3-8.4.

You can download it from http://www.taig.com/en/ for Windows and Mac.

For news, follow @TaiG_jailbreak.

How do I find my current version?

Open the Settings app, tap General, tap About, and look at Version.

(Your device's version is also listed at the bottom of the Cydia "homepage".)

shsh.title: Upgrading / Downgrading
shsh.body:
Can I downgrade/upgrade to the firmware version I want?

Probably not, and here's why.

Apple has a system that tries to make sure you can only install the latest iOS firmware version: devices require their firmware installation to be verified (signed) by Apple during every restore or upgrade. Apple usually only signs a version while it's the latest version. This is designed to keep you from installing jailbreakable versions as Apple fixes exploitable bugs.

It is possible to save your device's available SHSH blobs (signatures) for the current iOS version that Apple is signing, using a free tool called TinyUmbrella. You may do this in the hope that you can restore your device with those firmware versions later (after Apple no longer signs them), but there are few loopholes for using SHSH blobs on devices newer than iPhone 4 and on iOS versions newer than iOS 5. Apple has improved the security of their signing system over the past few years.

Cydia used to automatically save SHSH blobs for devices, when SHSH blobs were more usable. For explanation of that system, see Caching Apple's Signature Server (September 2009).

On devices newer than iPhone 4 and on iOS versions newer than iOS 5, SHSH blobs are usually not usable — in other words, you can only upgrade, downgrade, or restore to iOS versions that Apple is signing (which is usually only the newest iOS version available for that device).

redsn0w.title: redsn0w
redsn0w.body:
redsn0w is a tool for Mac and Windows that provides untethered jailbreaks for iOS versions including:

• iPhone 4S: 5.0, 5.0.1, and 5.1.1
• iPhone 4 (GSM): 4.1 through 4.2.1; 4.3.1 through 4.3.3; 5.0.1 and 5.1.1
• iPhone 4 (CDMA): 4.2.8, 5.0.1, and 5.1.1
• iPhone 3GS: 4.1 through 4.2.1; 4.3.1 through 4.3.3; 5.0.1 and 5.1.1 (old-bootrom iPhone 3GS is untethered on all versions)
• iPhone 3G: 4.1 through 4.2.1
• iPad 3rd generation: 5.1.1
• iPad 2: 5.0.1 and 5.1.1
• iPad 1: 4.3.1 through 4.3.3; 5.0.1 and 5.1.1
• iPod touch 3rd generation and 4th generation: 4.1 through 4.2.1; 4.3.1 through 4.3.3; 5.0.1 and 5.1.1
• iPod touch 2nd generation (which includes devices sold as iPod touch 3rd generation 8 GB): 4.1 through 4.2.1

And tethered jailbreaks for iOS versions including:

• iPhone 4 (GSM): 4.3.4 through 5.0, 5.1, and 6.0 through 6.0.1
• iPhone 4 (CDMA): 4.2.9 through 5.0, 5.1, and 6.0 through 6.0.1
• iPhone 3GS: 4.3.4 through 5.0, 5.1, and 6.0 through 6.0.1
• iPad 1: 4.3.4 through 5.0, and 5.1
• iPod touch 3rd generation: 4.3.4 through 5.0, and 5.1
• iPod touch 4th generation: 4.3.4 through 5.0, 5.1, and 6.0 through 6.0.1

redsn0w runs on already-upgraded un-jailbroken devices.

Steps: Download redsn0w for Mac or Windows. Open it, plug your device into your computer, and follow redsn0w's instructions.

If your version of iOS has a tethered jailbreak, this means you need to plug your device into a computer and run redsn0w every time your device boots (such as when it runs out of battery), or else it may get stuck at the Apple logo while booting — or it may boot up but in a seemingly "unjailbroken" state where Cydia and Safari will crash when you try to open them. To boot tethered: open redsn0w, click "Extras" and then click "Just Boot".

Tips for Windows users: Extract redsn0w.exe to your desktop instead of running it from inside the .zip archive. You may need to right-click redsn0w to run it from an administrator account and/or run it in XP compatibility mode. If you use Internet Explorer to download an IPSW file, you may need to change the file extension from .zip to .ipsw in order to use it.

Note for unlockers: if you upgrade iOS using iTunes, it will upgrade your iPhone's baseband, which negatively affects iPhones unofficially unlocked with ultrasn0w. Instead use redsn0w's "Custom IPSW" feature to upgrade and jailbreak your device while preserving your baseband. (Not currently possible on iPhone 4S.)

pwnagetool.title: PwnageTool
pwnagetool.body:
PwnageTool is a tool for Mac that jailbreaks iOS 5.1.1, 5.0.1, and 4.0 through 4.3.3 (on most devices except iPad 3rd generation, iPad 2, and iPhone 4S). It is able to preserve unlocked basebands.

Steps: Download PwnageTool. This will come in the form of an Apple disk image file. Copy PwnageTool to your hard disk before running it.

Use PwnageTool to make a Custom Firmware that can be used to Restore your device with iTunes.

When using this jailbreaking tool on iPhones unofficially unlocked with ultrasn0w, you should not check "upgrade the baseband".
